previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell degranulation syndrome was admitted for a typical flare characterized by shortness of breath, wheezing, chest pain, abdominal pain, pruritus, nausea, and vomiting. She presented after being unable to tolerate oral medications and had initially sought care at an outside hospital. Treatment included her established IV regimen of Dilaudid, Ativan, and diphenhydramine, along with albuterol nebulizers and supportive care. Labs showed mild leukocytopenia, likely related to immunosuppressive therapy, but no acute infection or organ dysfunction. Imaging revealed mild basilar atelectasis due to low lung volumes. Her symptoms gradually improved, and she was transitioned back to oral medications. No changes were made to her chronic regimen. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider and allergist.
problems: Other specified disorders involving the immune mechanism
Antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
